articleTitle: An Approach to Formation of Indicators for Assessing the Quality of Information Infrastructure Software Under the Conditions of the Destructive Impact of Cyber Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The authors propose an original approach to the formation of software quality indicators of the newly designed information and communication system of regional management, which allowed the authors to create a model for assessing the software quality of the regional management information and communication system and simulate the conditions of functioning of software under destructive impacts, and develop requirements for quality indicators and identify approaches to the software quality assessment process. The results of the experiment on modeling software quality indicators under destructive influences are presented.

articleTitle: Graph-Structural Modeling: Clique Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: Based on the click approach the interrelations of the type graph ↔ hypergraph, graph ↔metagraph, hypergraph ↔metagraph are established; their matrix characteristics are systematically used, namely the matrices of incidence, valence, adjacency and laplacian, as well as the canonical relation connecting them.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Conflict of the Opposing Sides in the Conditions of the Introduction of Hybrid Warfare with the Use of Cyber Weapons
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: At the turn of the 20th-21st centuries, the “fifth” dimension of hostilities appears in the theory of military art, and the arsenal of warfare is supplemented by new means of non-lethal influence, primarily by various types of information technology weapons. According to a number of scientists, the contribution to the result of the war is currently 1:4 in favor of non-military types of struggle. In this context, hybrid warfare has become a new type of interstate confrontation and an effective tool for strategic non-nuclear deterrence, exhaustion and isolation of the opposing State. Despite the fact that information technology weapons have been used for about twenty years, relatively recently these tools have become actively used in the conduct of hybrid wars. The existing scientific and methodological apparatus does not fully reflect the changed conditions for the use of a new type of weapon in hybrid wars. The article presents an approach that allows assessing the outcome of a hybrid war based on the application of an adapted Lanchester model of wars.

articleTitle: On the Order of Removing of Uncertainty Principles in the Problems of Possibilistic-Probabilistic Programming and the Evolutionary Method of their Solution*
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The paper investigates the linear programming problem in the context of hybrid uncertainty that combines uncertainties of possibilistic and probabilistic natures. With the help of constructive method using a numerical example we prove the noncommutativity of the order of application of decision-making principles to remove uncertainty. A genetic algorithm is specified for solving deterministic and stochastic analogues of the studied problems, which differ only in the order of application of decision-making principles to remove hybrid uncertainty.

articleTitle: The Influence of Shape Defects on the Spectrum of Natural Frequencies of a Cylindrical Resonator of a Solid-State Wave Gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: Using the finite element method, the dependence of the spectrum of natural frequencies of a cylindrical resonator of a solid-state wave gyroscope on the depth of the circular hole and the through slit on its top is calculated. An increase in the splitting of natural frequencies with an increase in the depth of these defects and the binding of the resonator axes to such defects has been established. The influence of the number of finite elements on the accuracy of calculation of natural frequencies was also studied

articleTitle: Simulation of Avalance-Threating Snow Mass Movement
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: Results of analysis and generalization of the possibilities in the known ways of simulation the movement of avalanche-threatening snow mass are presented in the work. 3D-model based on the dynamics of the particles was shown to provide a high degree of precision in the spatial and time discretization. In its turn, this ensures calculations of the movement trajectory, energy and avalanche pressure. Thus, the bulk discrete model of snow mass makes it possible to get an adequate assessment of the avalanche destructive effect.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation of the Surface Radiometry Process
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The problem of modeling the process of ocean radiotomography by means of passive or active radiosonding is considered. The possibility of restoring the shape of the ocean surface by the received signal and the influence of ocean surface disturbances on the process of restoration is investigated. The diffraction of electromagnetic radiation on a periodic layer is modeled using the method of parallel projections. A cluster supercomputer variant of the organization of computations by means of this method is implemented, the parallel properties of the algorithm are investigated. The speedup of the parallel implementation of computations on clusters MVS-10P, MVS-100K MSC RAS and HybriLIT LIT JINR turns out to be close to linear. For the needs of the ocean radiotomography, calculations are carried out to determine the optimal sensing angle; the possibility of solving the inverse problem of restoring the shape of the ocean surface from the radiosonding data is shown.

articleTitle: Developing Information Model of Blood Pressure Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The development of hospital information system requires the improvement of diagnostic and monitoring tools. The tools should provide extensive diagnostics and automatic data processing. The article deals with an information model for measuring blood pressure, compares experimental findings and presents a blood pressure measurement algorithm. The algorithm will allow to conduct an advanced monitoring of patients’ conditions considering their individual characteristics and without healthcare professionals directly involved. Implementing such an algorithm into hospital system will allow to urgently respond to the change in patients’ conditions.

articleTitle: Models and Algorithms to Support the Coordination of Socio-Economic Indicators of Regional Development in the Context of Epidemiological Restrictions
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The article is devoted to the development of mathematical models and algorithms for harmonizing regional development indicators in difficult conditions caused by the need to introduce epidemiological restrictions. Based on a systematic approach, the task of harmonizing the socio-economic indicators of the region's development under conditions of epidemiological restrictions is posed and formally described. This task has a two-level structure, which reflects the hierarchical system of the region. At the top level, regional authorities form a control influence on the economic system of the region, ensuring development indicators of enterprises in the region sufficient to achieve the required values of social indicators. At the same time, the interests of the management of enterprises in the region and the difficulties associated with additional costs and limited participation of labor resources in the production process (lower-level task) are taken into account. To specify the lower-level task, a model has been formed to determine the parameters of the rational functioning of a group of enterprises under the conditions of epidemiological restrictions. Based on the model, an algorithm has been developed for harmonizing indicators of the socio-economic development of the region under the conditions of epidemiological restrictions. The algorithm makes it possible to find a solution to the coordination problem in the event that subsidies are chosen as a support measure by regional authorities. A software product has been developed to carry out practical calculations.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Interval-Valued Numbers in the Evaluation of Uncertain Parameters of the Investment Projects
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: Management of real investments is one of the key activities of modern enterprises. Real investments, especially those related to the formation of new capital (new companies, new production facilities), are associated with various types of uncertainty. This paper proposes to use the framework of fuzzy interval-valued numbers to model the uncertain parameters of the investment project and calculate the net present value. Fuzzy interval-valued numbers, which are often interpreted as fuzzy numbers of the second type (order) or super-fuzzy numbers, make it possible to model not only the value uncertainty on the base axis (carrier) of a certain parameter, but also the uncertainty associated with the value of the membership function. The paper proposes an algorithm for estimating the net present value of a project based on operations with fuzzy interval-valued numbers.

Author Keywords: Fuzzy interval-valued numbers of the second type
The effectiveness of the investment project

articleTitle: Optimal Cybersecurity Management of an IP Video Surveillance System
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The purpose of the study is to solve the urgent problem of building a system for protecting IP video surveillance computer networks used in the work of situational centers of law enforcement agencies from the spread of computer viruses. A mathematical model for protecting a computer network from malicious code was built based on the MSEIRS model. This model is versatile and universal, as it takes into account many factors that influence the state of the network: time parameters of infection for specific viruses and treatment of the network using an antivirus, the average speed of immunization and involuntary disconnection of computers from the network. The result of the study of the model is a developed program that allows you to assess the security of an IP video surveillance network and, if necessary, apply effective methods to combat the spread of computer epidemics. Computational experiments were carried out and analyzed. For this purpose, two cases are considered: the spread of the virus (epidemic) progressing over time and network and the absence of significant fluctuations in the number of infected computer network nodes.

articleTitle: Implementation and Research of Finite Element Method for Nonlocal Elasticity Theory Problems in Julia Programming Language
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The article proposes an implementation option for a finite element software package written in the Julia programming language that solves three-dimensional nonlocal elasticity theory problems. The article discusses the main features of the nonlocal theory and the implementation algorithm, taking into account the Julia language features. A number of calculations and comparisons of classical and nonlocal theories are carried out on the example of the problem of applying a load to the rigidly fixed beam end.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Error of Two-Dimensional Fast Trigonometric Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: Fast trigonometric interpolation of functions of two variables is considered. Compact formulas for determining the Fourier coefficients of fast expansions are written. The absolute error of approximation Δ of the function and its partial derivatives to the fourth order is investigated for a different number of terms of the Fourier series N. Computational experiments have shown that with an increase in N, the accuracy of the approximation of the function and its partial derivatives increases. With an increase by one term of the Fourier series from two to three and from three to four, the maximum value of the absolute error Δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>decreases by an order of magnitude. When approximating partial derivatives Δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>increases by an order of magnitude with an increase in the order of the partial derivative by one.

articleTitle: The Multicriteria Analysis Efficiency Method of Group Monitoring System Based on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicles system application for solving problems of group monitoring in extreme conditions is considered. The multicriteria analysis efficiency method of group monitoring system based on unmanned aerial vehicles is proposed. The multicriteria analysis is based on the assessment of the unmanned aerial vehicles number influence on the performance indicators of the monitoring system: reliability, timeliness and functional stability. An example of using regression analysis methods to determine the timeliness model parameters is given. Similarly, recognition reliability model parameters of observation objects can be determined. The unmanned aerial vehicles optimal number for the monitoring system using the multicriteria generalized objective function method has been determined.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Seismodynamics of an Extended Pipeline in Liquefiable Soil
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The problem of the impact of a longitudinal non-stationary seismic wave on an underground extended pipeline is considered, taking into account the destruction of soil structure and its transition to a liquefied state. On the basis of experimental data, it is assumed that when the value of shear stress at the pipeline-soil contact points is exceeded, structural destruction of soil begins. After completion of the destruction process, the soil passes into a liquefied state, determined by the coefficient of dynamic viscosity. The statement of the problem is math-ematically formulated for a piecewise linear approximation of the law of soil interaction with the pipeline. The problems are solved by the explicit finite differences method. In the interaction model during the transition from one state to another, iterative refinement of the solution to the problem is performed. The analysis of the results obtained is conducted and the influence of structural destruction and soil liquefaction on the wave process in the pipeline is shown.

articleTitle: Brute-Force Integer Max Flow Algorithm for Networks Under Reachability Restrictions
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: An exact algorithm for solving integer maximum flow problem under reachability restrictions is proposed. A computational complexity of brute-force method was obtained. Presented examples show main issues arising while solving network flow problems under reachability restrictions. Enhancements for reducing operations number and redundant computations are provided. Tree-structured networks are considered with respect to reachability restrictions. It is shown that the maximum flow problem can be solved in polynomial time for these networks.

articleTitle: Search for Clinical Entities Associated with Atherosclerosis Using Methods of Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: Natural language processing is one of the most important areas of machine learning aimed at extracting valuable information from documents that have a free-text format. With the help of this approach, it becomes possible not only to structure, order, and vectorize complex arrays of textual data, but also to use the obtained information for further stages of predictive and descriptive analysis. Currently, a number of effective models and algorithms of text processing have been developed, including those specific to the field of medicine, with Spark NLP being one of the most widely used frameworks in this area. This paper describes the approach to processing reports from the MIMIC-III database in order to search for diseases, treatment and diagnostics methods, associated with atherosclerosis.

articleTitle: Software Tool for Creating Semantic Models for the Russian Language
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: Development of automated text processing tools would be impossible without the results of many theoretical works in the field of linguistics. However, not all suggested methods, developed dictionaries, etc. are suitable for developing automated text processing applications without significant changes. The paper proposes a new approach to the use of semantic dictionaries within the set of text processing tools called “Framework TAWT”, describes the advantages of this approach, and provides the examples of solving computational linguistics problems using this approach.

articleTitle: Organization of Storage and Processing of Results from Industrial and Computational Experiments of Polymerization Processes Based on Databases
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The article presents an approach to storage and processing of results of large-scale chemical-technological experiments and computational experiments based on databases. The approach is presented on the example of isoprene polymerization processes in the presence of various microheterogeneous catalytic systems. A conceptual and logical database model of the study enterprise was created. The choice of catalytic system affects the number of types of active sites involved in the process; in the structure presented in this article, up to four types of active sites can be considered. The constructed structure can be adapted for other polymerization processes, depending on the type of the process, its formulation, and flow conditions. The presented physical model is implemented as a database and has been tested in the Microsoft SQL Server environment.

articleTitle: About the Formation of Polygonal Structures over the Rotating Disk
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The problem of viscous gas flow over a rotating disk is investigated using numerical simulation. The conditions in which axisymmetric flow is destroyed with the formation of almost regular polygonal structures are considered. With a fixed size of a disk rotating at the same speed, the viscosity and the thickness of the layer above the disk determine the flow. The flow maps with a sequential change from an octagon to a quadrilateral were obtained as a result of numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Application of Virtual Antenna Arrays Technology to Minimize the Influence of Soil Characteristics on the Direction-Finding Quality
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The paper considers the electrodynamic modeling of the radio direction-finding complex with the possibility of forming a “virtual” antenna array based on the Hankel function. The results of the study show that the use of the technology of “virtual” antenna arrays can significantly reduce the direction-finding error even in conditions of various types of underlying surface (soil). The gain from using VAA is 1.69 times the standard deviation of the bearing. The results achieved show the effectiveness of the VAA method in complex direction-finding problems.

articleTitle: A Model for Selecting a Seller's Offer on a Marketplace in a Competitive Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: This article deals with the problem of the effectiveness of a Marketplace. The stakeholders of a Marketplace are buyers and sellers. The objects are the aggregate of homogeneous products. The effectiveness of the trading platform, which can be characterized by the number of transactions made, will depend on how adequate the sellers put up offers. The paper looks at mathematical models to support of decision-making of the seller in making such offers. Focusing not only on the buyer demand but also on the presence of competitors on the site is a distinguishing feature of the models. To describe the competition the apparatus of game theory is offered, namely the normal form of the game with a bimatrix model with two players: the seller - customer of service and the coalition of other sellers.

articleTitle: Searching Algorithm for Scientific Articles about COVID-19
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The article discusses a new method of accelerated search of scientific articles on coronavirus, as well as reflections on creating a search engine for specialists in the field of COVID-19. The necessity of improving algorithms for searching this information is caused by the need of creating thematical search tools for medical personnel who are developing medications against various strains of coronavirus. The goal is to create an algorithm for the search of semantic signs among scientific articles in English and to deliver the relevant search results. The Latent Dirichlet placement was used as a method of preliminary data processing. Jensen-Shannon metric was chosen for semantic comparison. In the result of the research, there were given system answers to the typical questions formulated by virologists.

articleTitle: Undecidability of Unary Unnested PFP-operators for One Successor
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: We continue to investigate semantics of the partial fixed point for infinite algebraic structures. We consider the following definition: a partial fixed point operator is true on those tuples those belong to the relation at almost every step. For this operator, we show that the halting problem for a Minsky machine is reducible to the problem of the truth of partial fixed point logic formulas for the one successor function theory. We establish this result in the case when formulas contain no more than one PFP-operator, and this PFP-operator is unary, and its inner formula is universal.

articleTitle: ARIMA–LSTM Method for Predicting Natural Systems Patterns Using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The paper presents an analysis of the problem of time series forecasting. The two most common forecasting methods, ARIMA and LSTM, are considered. Since these models independently predict linear and, accordingly, nonlinear dependencies in the best way, a hybrid model is considered using both initial methods in order to combine their strengths, improved by a genetic algorithm for automated model parameterization. A software implementation is built and advantages are described in relation to the original methods based on datasets with different trend, seasonal, non-linear components. In result, an integrative model was compared with ARIMA and LSTM models on 3 datasets and got better results by 6.33% and 8.36% respectively.

articleTitle: Predicting the Optical Power of Intraocular Lenses by Means of Dynamically Developing Artificial Intelligence System
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The article studies the possibility of using mathematical models obtained as a result of deep learning of artificial neural networks (ANN models) to predict the optical power of state-of-the-art intraocular lenses (IOLs), widely used in the surgical cataract treatment in ophthalmology. A distinctive feature of such ANN models in comparison with the well-known formulas SRK II, SRK/T, Hoffer-Q, Holladay II, Haigis, Barrett is their ability to take into account a significant number of recorded input quantities, which makes it possible to reduce the mean relative error in calculating the optical power of IOL from 10-12% to 3.5%. ANN models have been trained on large-scale samples including depersonalized data for 455 patients. The resulting models, in contrast to the traditionally used formulas, reflect the regional specificity of patients largely. They also make it possible to retrain and optimize the structure based on newly received data taking into account the nonstationarity of the object. The results obtained allowed to build a dynamically developing artificial intelligence system for predicting the optical power of intraocular lenses with a continuous flow of new data from a source and a step-by-step retraining of the ANN model.

articleTitle: The Effect of the Combination of Basis and Functional on the Results of DFT-calculation of Atomic Structure of Silicon-Hafnium Anionic Clusters
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The paper analyzes the influence of the functional and the basis on the results of calculations to optimize the atomic structure of silicon-hafnium clusters in the terms of the density functional theory. Anionic clusters <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{HfSi}_{\mathrm{n}}^{-}$</tex> (n =14-17) were selected as the object of test calculations. The combinations of the most popular B3LYP, B3PW91 and PBE functionals are compared in combination with three basic sets each - 6-311+g(d), aug-cc-pvdz and SDD. The criterion for assessing the adequacy of the calculation method is the comparison of the calculated electronic spectra of various cluster isomers with experimental photoelectron spectra.

articleTitle: Medication Adherence in Cardiovascular Disease Using Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: There is a growing interest in the use of research results aimed at improving the quality of medical care. Compliance with the instructions prescribed by the doctor is one of the factors that determines the positive result of treatment. This article describes the results of a study of factors affecting the compliance of patients in a cardiological hospital. Based on machine learning methods, a model for predicting the regularity of taking prescribed medicines has been built. With the help of modern methods of interpretation of modelling results, the hidden relationships between the patient's adherence to therapy and various clinical and physiological factors have been identified

articleTitle: Comparison of Heuristic Strategies for Sugar Beet Processing Schedules
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The article considers heuristic strategies of processing batches of sugar beet taking into account their uneven degradation. The processing sequence affects the amount of output of sugar. The purpose is to maximize the sugar yield. The optimization problem is closely related to the well-known assignment problem of discrete optimization. Various heuristic strategies have been proposed to achieve the stated purpose. To evaluate the capabilities of different strategies, a numerical experiment was carried out. For known sets of initial sugar content and batch degradation parameters at each processing stage, the value of the objective function for each of the proposed strategies is calculated. After 50 such experiments, the average relative losses were calculated and tables of relative losses were built. The results obtained allow us to evaluate which strategy is preferable for this acceptable set of parameters, and which ones are not profitable to use exclusively. The results were analyzed and recommendations for practical implementation were drawn up.

articleTitle: Time-Fractional Approach for Numerical Simulation of Temperature-Dependent Hysteresis in Ferroelectrics
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The paper presents the time-fractional modification of the Landau - Ginzburg - Devonshire - Khalatnikov model to describe the dynamics of polarization switching and estimate temperature-dependent characteristics in ferroelectrics with the first order phase transition. The mathematical model is formal-ized by an initial-boundary value problem for a time-fractional cubic-quintic equation. To solve the problem numerically, we derived a computational scheme as a combination of an implicit finite-difference scheme and an iterative procedure. An application program was developed in Matlab to implement the designed computational algorithm. The special software allows one to predict and control the changes in polarization in polar dielectrics in different dynamical modes under variation of the order of the time-fractional derivative and time-dependent thermody-namic parameters. The results of computational experiments are discussed to assess temperature-dependent characteristics of polarization switching in BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>ferroelectric crystals.

articleTitle: Absorption of the Electromagnetic Radiation of the Pyrolyzed Polyacrylonitrile: Model in the 1 to 3 GHz Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: At the present time the electromagnetic characteristics of composite materials, including polymeric materials, are widely studied for the purpose of their application as radio absorbing coatings and in electronics. One of such materials is pyrolyzed polyacrylonitrile (PPAN). The paper presents a model of electromagnetic radiation absorption by a PPAN layer depending on the layer width and its electrical conductivity.

articleTitle: Fibonacci Model Unitary Subgroup Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: A permutation quantum computer model is used to describe a modern quantum computer. This approach suggests the use of knot theory as mathematics describing the processes of this model. To connect this model with the existing mathematics of special unitary operators, the idea was expressed to correlate special unitary operators with quaternions and introduce node algebra already on quaternions. Kauffman and Lomonaco described this approach by posing the question of the density of the resulting subgroup in a special unitary group.

articleTitle: Forecasting by Using the Bayesian Belief Network of the Activation and Probable Consequences of Hazardous Natural Processes
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The article proposes to model complex natural processes and forecast their catastrophic consequences using the Bayesian belief network. The most significant factors that affect the activation of natural processes leading to catastrophic consequences are considered. It also reviews factors that can contribute to activation, but under certain additional conditions. A probabilistic model is built based on the Bayesian belief network, modeling is carried out. Various scenarios of complex natural processes with catastrophic consequences are considered. A control factor is proposed that affects the natural system and has a deterrent effect. The cyclical nature of the activation of natural processes associated with the solar activity is revealed.

articleTitle: Method of Interval Assessment of Information Efficiency of Network Infocommunication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: Work is devoted to development of a method of interval assessment of information efficiency of network infocommunication systems on the basis of the generalized indicator – coefficient of useful use of opportunities of a system on transfer and storage of information. The analysis of well-known approaches to estimation of efficiency of information of exchange of network infocommunication systems as a result of which the relevance of interval assessment for definition of the conditions of information of exchange allowing to use rationally channel and network of resources at the level close to potential opportunities on transfer and storage of information is formulated is carried out. For this purpose, at the first stage the technique of formation of function of information efficiency as dependences of coefficient of useful use on intensity of input traffic is developed. Then at the second stage the threshold level of coefficient of useful use which forms criterion for realization of interval assessment is reasonable and determined. Imitating modelling of the developed method for toroidal structures of network infocommunication systems in the conditions of change of input traffic is carried out. The received results confirmed capacity for work of the offered method. Practical recommendations about use of a method in tasks of assessment of information efficiency and adaptation of network infocommunication systems to the changing operating conditions are formulated.

articleTitle: Computer-Assisted Approach to Study of Bacterial Communication for Landau-Based Model of Population Growth
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: This paper proposes a mixed deterministic model of bacterial communication process during bacterial colony growth in nutrient media. The model formalization includes a combination of the reaction-diffusion quorum sensing model and the bacterial evolution model related to the Landau theory within the core framework of the existence of a growth threshold for bacteria in the growth process. To solve the application problem, the finite element method was used. The implementation was done on the COMSOL Multiphysics platform. Taking the Pseu-domonas putida bacterial species as an example, computational experiments were performed to examine the spatial-temporal characteristics of the biological system. The obtained results confirm that the considered approach can help to predict the growth morphology of bacterial colonies and control the dynamic process of bacterial communication to a certain extent.

articleTitle: On the Problem of Portfolio Optimization with Constraints on Possibility/Necessity - Probability and Probability - Possibility/Necessity
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: In this paper we investigate models of minimum risk portfolio under hybrid uncertainty of possibilistic-probabilistic type. To remove two levels of uncertainty, constraints on possibility/necessity-probability and probability-possibility/necessity are used. Equivalent deterministic and equivalent stochastic models are constructed for the case when random components are normally distributed, and methods for solving the result problems are provided. The applicability of these methods are demonstrated on numerical examples.

articleTitle: Reflective Phase Shifter Based on Active Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The paper proposes a design of a reflective phase shifter based on an active metamaterial. On the basis of the performed electrodynamic modeling, the main parameters of the phase shifter were calculated, as well as the patterns of the electromagnetic field. The obtained dependences show the effectiveness of the proposed metamaterial structures for controlling the phases of electromagnetic waves at the output of the structure, while it is possible to achieve a wide range of phase changes, small losses in the process of switching the operating modes of the structure.

articleTitle: Application of Computational Theory of Semantic Interpretation to Detect Cybercrime
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The article describes an approach to detect a cybercrime by identifying semantic objects in Russian text. The identification is based on the theoretical principles of the computational theory of semantic interpretation, which uses the computational representation of the semantics of texts and the comparison of texts for semantic similarity. The proposed approach reveals the semantic traces of objects in text. The focus is on the search for and prevention of cybercrime such as the inclination of adolescents and juveniles to commit suicide. All examples provided in the paper are provided for the Russian language. For the sake of convenience, a translation into English language is provided.

articleTitle: Detecting Graphic Objects Using an Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The article considers an approach to editing graphic objects (for example, road signs) using artificial layered convolutional neural networks. A mobile road laboratory “TRASSA” was used as engineering equipment for collecting information. The experimental results demonstrate high accuracy of identification of road signs in different environments. An object recognition approach using deep machine learning is described, in which a convolutional neural network is used and software for identifying road signs is developed. The suggested approach makes it possible to discover the existence of detectable objects in data flows and to identify them on this basis.

articleTitle: Modeling of Extended Flooding of the Volga-Akhtuba Floodplain Under Various Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: A computer model of a extended flood due to an accident at a hydraulic structure is considered. The model is based on the two-dimensional Saint-Venant equations, taking into account the friction and the structure of the terrain on the right side. The integration of the equations is carried out using the Lagrangian-Eulerian CSPH-TVD method (Combined Smooth Particle Hydrodynamics - Total Variation Diminishing). Modeling of various scenarios of the destruction of the Volga hydroelectric dam on the dry bottom during the fall and the wet bottom during the seasonal flood was carried out. For calculations, a regular digital terrain model is used, taking into account the channels of the Volga, Akhtuba and the main floodplain peaks. The main parameters of the breakout wave are calculated. Integral characteristics of flooding for the northern part of the Volga-Akhtuba floodplain are obtained. It is shown that hydraulic friction influences the propagation velocity of the breakthrough wave. The simulation results for a given digital model confirm the hypothesis that Volgograd is located in a zone that is not subject to flooding.

articleTitle: Phase Trajectories of Linear Homogeneous Autonomous Dynamical Systems of the Third Order
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The proposed article is devoted to the study of the problem of constructing phase trajectories in the vicinity of a singular point. This paper presents a more expanded view of this problem in comparison with those previously considered by other authors and suggests a more meaningful and grounded development of this study. Numerous examples of the application of this approach to the study of trajectories at a singular point are given.

articleTitle: Computer DFT-Experiment to Study the Possibility of the Existence of Anionic “Superatoms” MeSnn– (Me=Sc, Y, La; n=12, 16,20)
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The paper analyzes the possibility of the existence of stable MeSn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> (n=12, 16, 20) “superatoms” stabilized by scandium, yttrium or lanthanum atoms. Optimized structures of several stable isomers of clusters are presented. The influence of the type of encapsulated metal atom on the stability of a closed structure of tin atoms is considered. Computer modeling in the terms of density functional theory is used for research.

articleTitle: Applied Aspects of Number Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The article deals with the applied aspects of number theory related to the exponentiation modulo algorithm. This algorithm has found application in the RSA cryptosystem. The method of increasing the level of protection of the asymmetric RSA algorithm is proposed. To increase the level of protection, the RSA algorithm is supplemented by generating the pseudorandom primes with a large modulo. This solution excludes decomposition into continuous fractions when trying to find the RSA private key. Modeling of the asymmetric cryptosystem is done in the Wolfram Mathematica computer environment. To simulate this process, a reversible one-dimensional cellular automaton is used. This structure corresponds to rule 15. The work of the cellular automaton is based on the logical operation of the sum modulo two. To assess the vulnerability of the cryptosystem, an attack by Michael Wiener is embedded in the program code.

articleTitle: Elementary Theoretical Model of Thermal Breakdown Generation in Semiconductor Film
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: It is proposed an elementary theory of thermal breakdown of functional element in electrical circuit. It is represented in the form of the film on the basis of semiconductor material. The theory is based on a simple mathematical model which takes into account the balance of heat between thermal channels originated temperature deviations. Each of them is a self-consistent heat source due to an electric current flowing through the film. Such channels located perpendicular to the film. The positive feedback between the heating of the thermal channel and the current growth in it leads to super-fast growth of the temperature in such a channel up to the melting temperature. Such an evolution process is interpreted as a thermal breakdown of the material. It leads to the formation of melting channels with small diameter which are directed through the film. In turn, it leads to degradation of the electrical properties of the material.

articleTitle: Parallel Implementation of 3D Model of Wave Hydrodynamics and its Verification*
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The research delves into parallel algorithms for implementing a three-dimensional wave hydrodynamics model through MPI technology in software. The scalability of the proposed algorithms is assessed, and metrics are computed to gauge the efficiency of parallel computing. Verification of the mathematical model is conducted, and simulation results are compared with those from contemporary third-generation wind-wave models (WAM, SWAN, WaveWatch). Numerical experiments, utilizing input data from WorldView satellite images of the Azov Sea, are presented and juxtaposed between SWAN and the three-dimensional wave hydrodynamics model. The image contours are identified using the Local Binary Patterns (LBP) method. Information about the sea bottom bathymetry is derived from the Taganrog Cadastre Bureau data, and a bitmap image of the bottom section is generated for its incorporation into the model..

articleTitle: Features in Aerodynamic Characteristics and Flow Structures Around an Aircraft with Perforated Stabilizing Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The paper is devoted to mathematical modeling of subsonic airflow around a high aspect ratio aircraft with stabilizers in a wide range of angles of attack from 0° to 90°. The stabilizers were thin flat perforated plates. The study of interference that occurs between the body of the aircraft and the stabilizing devices is the focus of the paper. The commercial computational package FlowVision was chosen as a tool for the numerical experiment. It makes it possible to carry out numerical simulations of the flow around vehicles of various shapes and layouts with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Conditions of Application of the Modified Least Square Method for Models Identification of Distributed Dynamic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The identification of the parameters of distributed dynamical systems is an important task for technical, economic and social applications. The quality of statistical estimates is usually determined by two criteria: standard error and bias. But most of the methods cause the inconsistency of the criteria. The desire to reduce the standard error generates an increase in bias and vice versa, such a problem is well known in machine learning. The paper proposes a modified least squares method (OLS), the use of which provides a reduction in both criteria. The conditions for its application are considered.

articleTitle: System Analysis of Multi-Factor Authentication Methods to Improve the Security of Access to Data in an IT Company's Information System
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: Recently, more and more companies are spending huge budgets and implementing various technologies to protect their information from unauthorized access. One such technology is two-factor authentication. This type of authentication has become a kind of trend in IT companies. It does not mean a simple “Login / Password” method, but the presence of a certain unique identifier, thanks to which you can log into user accounts. This article describes the new model and the basic steps you need to take to implement a two-factor authentication model for an organization.

articleTitle: Identification and Accounting of Aperiodic Anomalies in Time Series with Cyclic Components
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: This article is devoted to solving the problem of studying time series with aperiodic point anomalous changes in the level values of the series. In addition, these series contain a cyclic component. The use of classical mathematical methods leads to obtaining models with unacceptable accuracy. The article developed methods for modeling time series with anomalous changes. The developed methods are based on the detection and exclusion of anomalous changes in the values of the series levels. In this case, the anomalous values of the levels of the series are subdivided into structural and parametric ones. An indicator method for detecting structural anomalies has been developed. And the detection of parametric anomalies is based on the assumption of the normality of the law of distribution of the values of the cyclic component with point exceptions of the levels of the series. To solve the problem, cyclic and trend components were identified at intervals of non-anomalous changes in level values.

articleTitle: Threshold Wavelet Filtering of Images Based on Weight Model
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: Many modern information processing and control systems are based on computer vision technologies. In such systems, a number of tasks are solved, including the task of primary image processing. The primary processing is designed to transform the geometric, brightness and color characteristics of images, ensuring that they are brought to the best possible appearance for further analysis. Brightness conversion must be performed to implement image enhancement and restoration procedures. Threshold wavelet filtering is the basis of one of the frequently used approaches for solving these problems. To build the appropriate procedures in this article, it is proposed to use a weight model of the image. This model allows us to obtain estimates of the significance of the contribution of pixels to the total energy of the analyzed image.

articleTitle: Computer Decision Support System for Resource-Saving Polymer Extrusion Design Based on Virtual Models
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: A computer decision support system for the design and change-over of production of multi-assortment polymeric materials has been developed. The system helps to solve the problems of choosing hardware design and technological modes of extrusion, ensuring resource saving in production. The system includes a subsystem for selecting the brand of the extruder and assembling a 3D model of the modular screw of the extruder, a subsystem for synthesizing a mathematical model for calculating the extrusion efficiency indices depending on the operating parameters of the extruder, a database of types of polymeric materials, a database of brands of extruders, a database of technological regulations of extrusion. 3D models of elements of screw extruders of various types, rules of placement and layout of 3D models of elements when assembling a 3D screw model, mathematical models of physical processes in the channels of screws and heads of extruders are the core of the system. The system allows you to select the brand of the extruder, form the configuration of the extruder screw and determine the operating parameters of extrusion, at which the specified requirements for the quality of the extrudate, throughput and specific energy consumption of the extrusion are satisfied. Testing of the system has been carried out according to the data of industrial extrusion and calendering productions of multi-assortment polymeric films for packaging food and medicines. The test results have confirmed the operability of the software. They have showed an increase in production efficiency due to a reduction in defective products (non-returnable waste), energy saving, and a reduction in the time of change-over of production on new tasks.

articleTitle: Formalization of the Concept of Relationship for Qualitative Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The article considers the possibility of studying data about the environment through relationships that have not been given appropriate attention due to the vagueness and diversity of the utilization of this term. Even before the realization of the proposed formalization, a specific set of relations was used in structuring the flow of amplitudes. This opened up the possibility of solving many problems related to the analysis and synthesis of the information content of various types of waves. The formalization of the concept of relations has revealed a whole layer of representatives of such relations, the interpretation and use of which is yet to come. For some types of relations, it was possible to obtain an estimate the number of possible combinations of of the field relation configurations depending on the number of participating sets. All this is described in the proposed presentation.

articleTitle: On the Implemention of the System-Biological Approach in Modeling the Functioning of Degenerative Diseases Biomarkers
publicationTitle: 2023 Applied Mathematics, Computational Science and Mechanics: Current Problems (AMCSM)
abstract: The basic minimal mathematical models of the general type system functioning p53-protein-inhibitor-microRNA for the class of microRNAs with a positive direct connection and a positive feedback are proposed and justified by comparisons with the experimental data. This system is an idealization of a number of segments of the p53 protein signaling pathway, which controls the cellular response to damage and cell death programs. The interrelation is numerically shown between the basic models and the models of the functioning of the system as a multi-stage process of transmitting a biochemical signal with a linear representation of intermediate fast-flowing stages.
